rows.rationale: The complete spatial adjective entry gives medius and cites Hen.18,8; source has a third-person singular suffix. Preserve that suffix rather than silently writing a plural pronoun or adding mountain. Grammar pp.339–341 and 354–357 supplies suffix formation; a one/part sense is implicit in substantival middle, not an added source noun.

The complete verb entry gives percutere/pulsare and separately trudere, protrudere, explicitly citing Hen.18,8. Here with a spatial limit, jut/project is the bounded spatial sense. Native verb plus Table I u-containing Gamal distinguishes ጐ from ordinary ጎ.
The complete preposition/conjunction entry includes usque ad and spatial terminus. Source carries a raised asterisk before this word; the star is editorial and is not a fidel.
The complete entry gives coelum; no plural form is substituted for this printed singular.
Complete entry includes comparative ut, sicut, quemadmodum, quasi. This is a comparison, not a declaration that the formation literally is a divine throne.

Complete entry gives sedes, solium, thronus among senses. Both throne tokens end with the native Rees I shape, not Rees II; the comparative throne sense fits the explicit Lord relation without borrowing an English Enoch text.

Complete divine-name entry explains dominus ... universi and use as the proper name/title of God. The prefix la is kept as for rather than suppressed. Complete la entry covers directional, beneficial and general relational functions.

Complete stone entry gives lapis; final a marks the source construction. Relative za plus em expresses which is of/from. Complete em entry explicitly includes materia, ex qua aliquid fit vel componitur; the relative attaches to the throne phrase, not the Lord.

The actual full entry in col.1392, not merely a head match, explicitly cites Hen.18,8 and gives album marmor, fortasse alabastrites. It notes another cited item differs. The entry ends before the next head; the next photographed page begins the lexicon appendix, not an omitted semantic continuation. Native source Pa/Psa order V matches Table I; pă/pe/pə is not guessed from English. Retain a transparent stone-name rather than assert a modern mineral identity.

Complete photographed entry gives vertex et caput and cites Hen.18,8. Native second fidel has the right extension of Dant VI, not Dant I; actual Yaman VI and same-page Y control differ. Final Haut II retains root consonant plus third-person singular u. Thus reject the preserved failed ወደማሑ reading, not by lexical expectation or model vote.

Read the printed la prefix and Rees I ending, not an assumed u suffix. La can introduce the relational noun after a preceding suffixed noun; complete la entry describes its general relation and use with anticipatory suffixes. The source literally retains summit/its plus la-throne; top of the throne renders that relation without changing throne to mountain.
The second stone construction repeats em plus stone, with an English copula supplied for the nominal predicate. Do not invent an additional source verb or qualitative modifier.

The complete actual entry in col.375 gives sapphirus and explicitly cites Hen.18,8. The name is represented as sapphire in its historical lexical sense, without certifying a modern gemological identification.

whole_scope: All 13 printed words, conjunctions, prefixes/suffixes, comparison, spatial limit, both stone constructions, and full explanatory footnotes were audited by this new informed author. This is not an independent peer review, whole chapter approval, manuscript collation, or publication approval.
